summary: Independent audit of supervisor/solve-geometry/AMPLIFIER.md (frozen, hash-identical). Core claim survives, one false lemma. (1) Lemma 1 ('the whole chain is monochromatic') is FALSE: only the ANCHORS are forced equal. Counterexample at k = 2, n = 3: gadget the path p-(1/8,3sqrt7/8)-q, d = 1/4, n* = 3, D = 3/4; C_3 is a 7-point path whose two 2-colourings give all p_i one colour and all r_j the other, so c(r_0) != c(p_0). The theorem survives (its proof uses only end-equality); corrected Lemma 1' supplied. (2) Accident class (4) is MISSING from section 5: accidental unit distances between distinct copies of the SAME chain; harmless for the lower bound, not for (H4) or the nE count. (3) The k=3 validation is correct (Moser spindle) but runs at n*=1, so it exercises no chaining. (4) Corrected Theorem A: under (H1)+(H2) with D >= 1/2, X is not k-colourable; D > 1/2 is sufficient, not necessary, and no accident hypothesis is needed. (5) A new n = 3 instance confirms the full theorem including (H4): |X| = 13, |E(X)| = 13 = 2nE+1, field Q(sqrt7,sqrt5) as predicted. (6) Absence of a forcing pair is only NECESSARY for chi(R^2) <= 6.

verified_results.statement: Frozen read copy: audit-amplifier/AMPLIFIER.frozen.md, sha256 492bcae4..., byte-identical to supervisor/solve-geometry/AMPLIFIER.md as read this block.

Theorem A (corrected lower bound, re-derived): under (H1) and (H2), with d = |p-q| > 0, D = n d >= 1/2 and X = C_n u R_theta C_n as defined in the file, X is not k-colourable. No coincidence or accident hypothesis is required, since the argument uses only C_n subset X, the anchor equalities of Lemma 1', and the single final unit edge.
verified_results.grade: PROOF (mine; supersedes the file's version only in its scope, which is wider)

verified_results.statement: Lemma 1 of the file ('in every proper k-colouring all points of the chain have the same colour') is FALSE. Corrected Lemma 1': only c(p + i d u) = c(q + i d u) for each i, hence c(p) = c(p+d u) = ... = c(p + n d u); other points are unconstrained.

Counterexample to Lemma 1 at k = 2 with n = 3: G = {(0,0), (1/8, 3sqrt7/8), (1/4,0)} (a path, bipartite, so (H2) holds at k = 2), d = 1/4, n* = 3, D = 3/4. C_3 is a 7-point path p_0-r_0-p_1-r_1-p_2-r_2-p_3; in both 2-colourings all p_i share one colour and all r_j the other, so c(p_0) = c(p_3) but c(r_0) != c(p_0).
verified_results.grade: EXACT computation (Q(sqrt5,sqrt7), Fractions) + proof; edge set equal to the 6 within-copy edges

verified_results.statement: Section 5's accident list omits a fourth class: accidental unit distances between distinct copies of the same chain (pairs x + i d u, y + j d u, i != j, distance exactly 1). Section 5.1 covers only distance 0 (coincidences). It cannot weaken the lower bound but does affect the (H4) gluing and makes nE only a lower bound.
verified_results.grade: gap identified; NOT exhibited in the instance built (all 6 edges there are within-copy)

verified_results.statement: The file's D > 1/2 requirement is sufficient but not necessary: at D = 1/2, theta = pi, the far ends are D u and -D u at distance 2D = 1 and Theorem A applies unchanged. D >= 1/2 is sharp (a chord of length 1 on radius D needs 2D >= 1).

Section 7's Moser-spindle validation is correct: d = sqrt3, cos theta = 5/6, sin theta = sqrt11/6, K' = Q(sqrt3, sqrt11), counts 7 vertices and 11 edges. But n* = 1 there, so it tests section 3 only and exercises no part of section 2's chaining (Lemma 1', the nV-(n-1) count, the coincidence classes).
verified_results.grade: re-derived by hand; limitation of the validation identified

verified_results.statement: New instance confirms the FULL theorem including the (H4) upper bound at n = 3: for the k = 2 gadget above, |X| = 13 = 2|C_3| - 1 with all points distinct, |E(X)| = 13 = 2nE + 1 exactly, |far1 - far2|^2 = 1 exactly, and the field is Q(sqrt7, sqrt5) = K(sqrt5) with 4n^2 d^2 - 1 = 5/4 exactly as section 6 predicts. So chi(X) = 3 = k+1.
verified_results.grade: EXACT computation; the <= direction argued from (H4) plus the exact edge-count equality, not by a colouring search

verified_results.statement: Overclaim in section 4: 'a negative answer to the forcing-pair question is exactly as hard as chi(R^2) <= 6'. Only the contrapositive is established (chi(R^2) <= 6 implies no forcing pair), so absence of a forcing pair is NECESSARY, not sufficient; no route from absence to an upper bound is given.

No forcing pair is asserted to exist, and none is found or claimed here. The construction yields a finite unit-distance graph, hence chi(R^2) >= chi(F); it is not a global structural statement about the plane.
verified_results.grade: scope statement, matches the file's own sections 0 and 8

conjectures: Accident class (4) will matter for any k = 6 gadget with d < 1/2, since chaining is then unavoidable; whether it can be avoided by choosing n is open.

The k = 2, n = 3 instance suggests the construction is genuinely robust at small k; a natural further check would be k = 3 with a gadget having d < 1/2, which needs a forced-equal pair at distance below 1/2 and so cannot be the diamond.
